recognize_zh: 箭頭處的紅血球比周圍正常紅血球大、顏色較淡，內含形狀不規則的阿米巴樣（amoeboid）寄生蟲，帶一顆紅色染色質點，胞質內可見細點狀薛氏小點（Schüffner dots），符合間日瘧（P. vivax）滋養體。
features: Single infected red cell enlarged and paler than surrounding uninfected erythrocytes
Irregular, amoeboid trophozoite with scattered blue-purple cytoplasm
Fine pink-purple stippling of the host cell consistent with Schüffner dots
Background erythrocytes normocytic without other parasites in this field; occasional platelets
describe_en: Thin peripheral blood smear shows a background of largely normocytic, normochromic erythrocytes. A single enlarged, pale red cell contains an irregular amoeboid trophozoite with a prominent chromatin dot and fine cytoplasmic stippling of the host cell (Schüffner dots). No banana-shaped gametocytes or multiply infected cells are seen in this field. Findings are consistent with a Plasmodium vivax trophozoite.

ddx.vs: P. falciparum rings are small and delicate in normal-sized red cells without Schüffner dots, often with multiple or appliqué forms, rather than a large amoeboid trophozoite in an enlarged cell.
P. ovale also enlarges the red cell with Schüffner dots, but the host cell is typically oval with fimbriated edges and the trophozoite is compact rather than amoeboid.
P. malariae infects normal-sized or small red cells without stippling and forms compact or band-shaped trophozoites.
A superimposed platelet lies in a different focal plane, has no halo of host-cell enlargement, and lacks a discrete chromatin dot with parasite cytoplasm.
